title: 4th Sitting of First session of 2026
summary: The sitting ran from 9:01 on Tuesday 17 February 2026 under Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim. After committee seat changes were announced and North Galolhu MP Mohamed Ibrahim introduced two bills and a resolution, the main business was the opening debate on the government's bill to amend the Employment Act, presented by Madaveli MP Mohamed Shameez. The bill covers notice for ending contracts, quota-fee relief for small and medium businesses and longer breaks for mothers. Seventeen members spoke: most government-side MPs backed it, while MDP members raised points such as notice periods, the length of the break, overtime on holidays and wider criticism of the government, and the debate was still running when this part ended with no vote. The part opens mid-speech on a bill the Chair then closed for debate because its sponsor was not in the chamber to reply, and continues with the preliminary debate on the government's National Service bill, where three MDP members questioned whether a one-year training and posting scheme would create jobs. Members then took up three committee reports: an Election Commission nominee, Maldives joining the OIC Labour Centre, and non-resident ambassadors to Cuba, Brazil and Mexico, with exchanges between MDP and PNC members that the Chair twice steered back to the report under discussion. At voting time 59 of 93 members were present and all six votes passed with no votes against: the bill went to the National Development and Heritage Committee and every nomination and the OIC Labour Centre accession were approved. The sitting ended with Ramadan greetings; the National Service bill debate was paused, not concluded, and the opening speaker's name is in part 1.

items.title: Independent Institutions Committee report on nominating Al-Ustaz Rifaath Abdulla (M. Wave, Kinara) to the Elections Commission
Foreign Relations Committee report on Maldives joining the Labour Centre of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) and ratifying its statute
Foreign Relations Committee report on non-resident ambassadors to Cuba, Brazil and the United Mexican States
items.outcome: debated; all three approved (Cuba 57-0, Brazil 58-0, Mexico 56-0)

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said some clauses, such as the Article 22(a) notice period and the 30-minute break, may not work in practice and should be improved in committee.
Raised complaints about staff transfers and Hulhumale' flat repairs.
On the National Service bill: asked how a year-long basic course followed by a posting would give youth jobs or skills, and noted the minister would decide placements.
Supported the OIC Labour Centre report as relevant to job security for his constituents.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Rebutted claims about judges being removed under MDP, saying majorities change over time.
Said promises on small-business support and replacing resort managers with Maldivians have not been acted on.
Argued fine waivers should reach everyone, and cited unpaid workers at a stalled harbour project.
Said the nominee is highly capable but doubted the Commission's independence when its leadership is appointed through a government-majority Majlis; also raised cost of living and election timing.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Backed the bill, saying paying wages through the full notice period (Article 25) benefits both sides.
Criticised MDP's record on jobs and payments and urged voters to turn out in the local council elections.
Supported the Elections Commission report, said the committee had done thorough work, and challenged opposition criticism, citing Sovereign Development Fund balances.
Supported the Foreign Relations Committee report on ambassadors and rebutted earlier opposition remarks on budgets and mosques.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Welcomed the changes to notice rules but asked how overtime on official holidays is treated and noted Labour Day is not listed as one.
Asked that his own amendment on resort service charges be scheduled.
On the National Service bill: said the Maldives lacks Maldivians to fill many jobs, but argued trainees would be better placed directly into existing industries and doubted the scheme's benefit.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported parts of the bill but said teachers and school staff lack overtime and allowances that other services receive.
In his second turn, disputed the North Mahchangolhi member's claims about MDP's record.
On the National Service bill: said he could not accept that this law would achieve the national vision, argued training belongs in the school system, and asked for the bill to be held for study.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Backed the bill, saying it tackles open-ended contracts, protects working mothers and eases quota fees for small and medium businesses.
Supported the OIC Labour Centre report as a way to secure workers' job security, and criticised remarks on the Sovereign Development Fund as off the report's subject.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Called the changes useful but stressed slow service to the public and proposed military training for school leavers before government jobs.
In his second turn, discussed the mothers' break clause and said remote-work technology gives working women flexibility; the speech continues into part 2.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Supported the amendments and asked the committee to extend the 30-minute break to one hour and cover men caring for sick relatives.
Accused MDP of opposing measures that help Male' residents.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Presented the OIC Labour Centre report, covering labour and social protection cooperation and the committee's unanimous vote to recommend it.
Presented the ambassadors report, saying the nominees meet the Foreign Service Act requirements and the committee recommended approval.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: On the ambassadors report: said atoll residents report shortages and hardship and questioned government spending relative to budgets passed.
Relayed island residents' complaints of idle equipment with expired warranties; the Chair reminded members to hear others patiently.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Presented the government's amendments: clearer rules for ending job contracts, quota-fee exceptions for some businesses, and longer breaks for mothers.
Said the changes make the labour market fairer and more attractive to foreign investors.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported all the amendments, citing Islamic teaching on keeping agreements and on doing work honestly and well.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Backed the bill, linking quota relief and clearer contracts to past foreign-labour problems for small businesses.
Urged action on harassment of women at work and on jobs for young graduates.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the bill, saying workers often go unpaid or lack overtime and that quota and notice changes help both sides; questioned MDP's silence on workers' rights.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Said the changes follow the President's meetings with businesspeople and ease quota burdens and notice rules for small firms.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Supported the bill as clarifying written agreements and notice for ending jobs, and as protecting both employers and employees.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Backed the bill, saying notice, quota and mothers' break changes respond to what people told the President, and rejected claims of hidden motives.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the bill as easing foreign-worker processing for small businesses and protecting mothers, and recalled a 2023 dismissal to rebut opposition claims.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Supported the amendments and asked the committee to lengthen the mothers' break to one hour.
Criticised MDP's record on dismissals and raised foreign crews on fishing boats.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Presented the committee report on the Elections Commission nominee, stating no public complaints were received and the nominee averaged 84.20% against the 75% threshold.

decisions: Committee seat changes were announced: Ibrahim Nazil replaces Hussain Ziyad, and Mauroof Zakir and Ahmed Shakir replace Ameen Faisal, from 11 February 2026.
Three items from North Galolhu MP Mohamed Ibrahim were introduced at first reading: two bills and a resolution.
Preliminary debate on the Employment Act amendment bill began but was not finished in this part; no vote was taken.
The Chair closed debate on the bill preceding item 7 because its sponsor was not in the chamber to give a closing reply.
Employment Act (Act 2/2008) amendment bill accepted 58-0 and sent to the National Development and Heritage Committee.
Al-Ustaz Rifaath Abdulla (M. Wave, Kinara) approved as an Elections Commission member, 58-0.
Maldives' accession to and ratification of the statute of the OIC Labour Centre approved, 58-0.
Non-resident ambassador to Cuba (Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed) approved 57-0.
Non-resident ambassador to Brazil (Dr. Ali Nasir Mohamed) approved 58-0; non-resident ambassador to Mexico (Shirzimath Sameer) approved 56-0.
The Chair ended the sitting after the agenda was completed, with Ramadan greetings.

votes.what: Accept the Employment Act (Act 2/2008) amendment bill for committee study (59 present of 93, 30 needed)
Appoint Al-Ustaz Rifaath Abdulla as Elections Commission member
Approve Maldives joining the OIC Labour Centre and signing its statute
Appoint Abdul Ghafoor Mohamed non-resident ambassador to Cuba (29 needed)
Appoint Dr. Ali Nasir Mohamed non-resident ambassador to Brazil
Appoint Shirzimath Sameer non-resident ambassador to Mexico
